classification.difficultyReason: Use an exterior angle to establish an opposite pair, apply the sine rule, then use right-triangle trigonometry without rounding the intermediate length.

content.prompt:
An archaeologist wishes to determine the height of an ancient temple. From a point $A$ at ground level, she measures the angle of elevation of $V$, the top of the temple, to be $37^\circ$.

She then walks $100\text{ m}$ towards the temple to a point $B$. From here, the angle of elevation of $V$ from ground level is $64^\circ$. Find:

spec.description: A, B and O lie on horizontal ground in that order, with V vertically above O. AV and BV meet at V. The 64-degree angle lies between BV and BO, exterior to triangle AVB. A right-angle square marks BOV. Ordinary source blue geometry uses house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle VAB is 37 degrees; angle VBO is 64 degrees; angle BOV is 90 degrees. AB is 100 m, given only in the stem.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and vertex labels appear; no calculated angles, lengths or height are shown.

answer.worked:
The exterior angle at $B$ equals the sum of the opposite interior angles of $\triangle AVB$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB+37^\circ&=64^\circ\\\angle AVB&=64^\circ-37^\circ\\\angle AVB&=27^\circ\end{align*}$$

Apply the sine rule in $\triangle AVB$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{VB}{\sin37^\circ}&=\frac{100}{\sin27^\circ}\\VB&=\frac{100\sin37^\circ}{\sin27^\circ}\\VB&\approx132.56\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: $OV$, the height of the temple, to the nearest metre

answer.short:
$119\text{ m}$

Use $OV=VB\sin64^\circ$, retaining the unrounded value of $VB$.
answer.worked:
In right-angled $\triangle BOV$, retain the exact expression for $VB$ from part b.
$$\begin{align*}\sin64^\circ&=\frac{OV}{VB}\\OV&=VB\sin64^\circ\\OV&=\frac{100\sin37^\circ}{\sin27^\circ}\sin64^\circ\\OV&\approx119\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
